Annie is notable not just as a woman sci-fi writer, but also as a lesbian with one black sister and another sister who is Vietnamese. She's the type of author the Puppies would NOT nominate if they were just aiming at pulp or the media's version of what the Puppies want: "white males shooting lasers in space."

I don't think it's a real thing. I think people idealize the concept of being put "in" a friendzone, but that the concept itself is not actually real. If you are not a romantic interest for a person, you were never in nor out of a friendzone. You were just not a romantic interest. If a non-romantic person advances romantic feelings towards a person who doesn't reflect those desires, you aren't being placed in a new zone, you were just never in a romantic context. This often happens when a person forms their relationship with someone as a good friend with no romantic undertones (reciprocity of touching, blushing, kissing, etc.). If there are no romantic inclinations, then the sudden assertion of romance from a person keeping it secret will of course seem like being put in a friendzone, but the friendzone never really existed as a thing to be put into.

You are either sexually involved with another person or you are not. Friendzone is an avoidance of the issue of reciprocated sexual tension.
